comments.content: The loop termination condition is incorrect when the received log length is exactly a multiple of `CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES`. If the last page returns exactly `CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES` entries (i.e., the log ends exactly at a page boundary), the loop will issue one extra query with `offset` equal to the total log length. That extra query returns an empty log, so it terminates correctly, but it's an unnecessary round-trip. More importantly, if the server-side cap is ever changed or the client's constant diverges from the server's, this could loop incorrectly. Consider breaking when `received_entries == 0` as well, or better, have the server return a flag indicating whether more entries are available.
